cpu_native.rss_note: one fresh process = interpreter + numpy + mujoco + 1 MjModel + 1 MjData. warp.workaround: mjm.opt.disableflags |= mjDSBL_MULTICCD (MJCF: <option><flag multiccd="disable"/></option>). Named in the error text itself. Only changes how many contacts mesh-mesh / box-mesh pairs produce (1 instead of several); foot-plane contacts are unaffected. Applied to BOTH the Warp model and the CPU reference in parity. Alternative from the same error text: zero the 1 mm geom margins (23 of 31 colliding geoms), which would also change foot-ground contact activation, so it was not used.

parity.summary: Yes, they diverge chaotically once contacts are involved, and there is also a systematic contact difference. (1) Systematic: at the identical seated start the contact sets already differ (CPU 10 vs Warp 6 contacts), so Warp-vs-CPU qpos differs by 8.8e-4 after 1 step and 8e-2 after 10 steps, far ahead of any round-off growth. (2) Chaotic: with contacts, tiny differences grow ~8 orders of magnitude in ~75 steps (0.15 s): two Warp worlds given bit-identical inputs start 5e-10 apart (MJWarp is not bitwise deterministic) and reach 1e-2 by step 75; CPU MuJoCo (bitwise deterministic run-to-run) moves 4e-3 by step 100 from a 1e-7 qpos perturbation. After ~100 steps Warp-vs-CPU (5e-2 to 1.2e-1), Warp-vs-Warp (1e-2 to 3e-2) and CPU-vs-perturbed-CPU (1e-3 to 5e-3) are within about an order of magnitude. (3) Without contacts there is no chaotic growth: Warp tracks CPU to 1.9e-4 over 400 steps (float32 drift) and Warp worlds agree to ~2e-6; muscle activations/tendon lengths/muscle forces match to float32 precision. Aggregate statistics (contacts/world, constraint rows, Newton iterations) agree closely. First look, not a verdict: trajectory-level parity is not attainable in this contact-rich regime; distribution-level parity looks plausible but untested.

interpretation_notes: At the seated initial pose CPU MuJoCo 3.14 returns 4 contacts per toes-plane pair (2 at -2.33 mm, 2 at +1.53 mm; both geoms have margin 1.0 mm) while MJWarp returns only the 2 penetrating ones; calcn-plane: 1 each on both. Constraint rows at step 1: CPU 68 vs Warp 52.
Contact-free: activation diff ~1e-8, tendon length diff <=6e-6 m, muscle force diff <=0.15 N (forces up to 3.4 kN) over 400 steps.

MJWarp is NOT bitwise deterministic: identical worlds (and two separate nworld=1 runs) differ from step 1 at ~1e-10; with contacts their contact counts differ in 57% of steps and qpos differs by ~1e-2 after 75 steps; the parity run's warp_cross_world_max_abs_diff (max over qpos/qvel/act/forces/tendon lengths and all 400 steps) is in muscle-force newtons. CPU MuJoCo repeated runs are bitwise identical.

notes: Stock models do NOT load in mujoco-warp 3.14.0 (exact error in warp.errors); a single option flag (MULTICCD off) makes them load and run.

Throughput: human_plus_hippo reaches 2.35M physics steps/s = 235k control transitions/s at nworld=8192 (3.6 GB GPU); the Hippo device costs ~5-8% vs the bare human on GPU (4.5% at nworld=8192) and ~2-3% on CPU.

Parity: trajectory-level agreement is not attainable with contacts (chaotic growth from round-off; MJWarp is not bitwise deterministic even run-to-run; plus a different contact set from step 1). Contact-free dynamics (muscles, spatial tendons, joint couplings) match to float32 precision. See parity.summary.
CPU: ~20.4-21.0k steps/s per thread (~2.0-2.1k transitions/s); 32 processes give 57.9k transitions/s (87% per-process efficiency).

Memory: human_plus_hippo loaded from XML costs ~560 MB RSS per process (93 MB MjModel, mostly the 8 high-res Hippo meshes, plus ~400 MB retained from compilation); loading a precompiled MJB brings it to ~153 MB.

Composed keyframes are not seated: human_plus_hippo key 'stand' has root z=1.000 while the MyoAssist-seated qpos0 has z=0.913, so resetting to key 0 (what myoassist_leg_base does) starts the model ~8.7 cm above the ground. All runs here start from qpos0.
The composed myolegs26 human has nkey=0; MyoAssist's leg env asserts nkey>0, so the bare human cannot be used there as-is (compose + Hippo adds 5 keyframes).
No <option> element in the composed XML: Euler, Newton (100 it, ls 50, tol 1e-8), pyramidal cone, dt=0.002 s.
Random excitation makes the model fall in ~0.9-1.0 s; workload per step ~6.3-6.7 contacts, ~66 constraint rows, ~1.8 Newton iterations (CPU and Warp agree).

Nothing was written outside the probe dir: ~/.cache, ~/.nv, ~/.local/share and ~ top level unchanged (CUDA_CACHE_PATH, WARP_CACHE_PATH, XDG_CACHE_HOME, UV_CACHE_DIR, TMPDIR, PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX all pointed inside it; PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 for the sprint venv). One .pyc in the sprint venv (dm_control/_render/__pycache__/glfw_renderer.cpython-312.pyc) was rewritten at 18:02:03 by another user of that venv; the probe's only use of it ended at 17:57:34 and a check right after showed zero changes; the probe never imports dm_control. /tmp/pytest-of-aurnab belongs to the other project's pytest run.
